lines.caption: What does it take to turn an empty folder… into an app that's live in Microsoft Fabric?
One command creates it, one runs it while you build, and one ships it. Watch!
Hi, I'm Ray! Welcome back to Learn Rayfin with Ray.
Today: how to create a Rayfin app, how to run it while you build, and how to ship it to Fabric. Let's dive in!

lines.said: First, what you need: NodeJS 20 or later and a Microsoft Fabric account.
lines.caption: First, what you need: Node.js 20 or later and a Microsoft Fabric account.
Fabric apps also have to be turned on in your tenant. A Fabric tenant admin flips that switch, so ask yours if it's off.
One command creates your app: npm create, with Rayfin's package and your app's name.
Keep the default template, the Universal App, and it installs your packages too.
Your app starts small: a website and sign-in. Its database stays off until your app needs one.
As it grows, add what it needs: your own data, connectors to data already in Fabric, functions, and file storage.
Next, sign in. rayfin login opens your browser, and you sign in with Microsoft Entra ID.
Then run npm run dev. In a Rayfin app, that runs rayfin dev.
When your frontend starts, it prints a local address. Open it, and there's your app.
Time for a deep dive! Your app is running… but where's its backend?
When rayfin dev starts, it finds your app’s backend in Fabric, or creates one the first time.
It applies your app's settings and data schema there, so the backend matches your code.
It writes the backend's address into your environment files, so the frontend knows where to call.
Then it starts your frontend, and any functions, right here on your machine.
So your backend lives in Fabric the whole time. There's no backend to run yourself.
And one thing rayfin dev never does is publish your frontend. That’s a job for rayfin up.
When you're ready to share, run rayfin up.
It builds your frontend for production, applies your settings and schema, deploys any functions, and publishes it all to Fabric.
The first time, it picks a workspace, checks its capacity, and creates your Fabric app there.
At the end, it tells you where your app is live. rayfin up status shows that address again, any time.
Here's the same journey in Fabricator. Choose New project, give it a name, and Fabricator runs npm create for you.
Next, deploy your app: sign in to Fabric, pick a workspace, and choose Deploy app.
Under the hood, that's rayfin login and rayfin up. And I talk you through it while it deploys.
When it's done, your app is live in the preview, and chat unlocks, so you can start building.
Pop quiz! Which command publishes your app's frontend to Fabric?
A, rayfin dev. B, rayfin up. Or C, rayfin login.
Pause the video, and guess…
It's B, rayfin up! rayfin dev runs your frontend on your machine, but never publishes it.
Let's recap. npm create starts your app from the Universal App. npm run dev runs it, with the backend in Fabric. And rayfin up ships it.
Your challenge: create a project in Fabricator, deploy it, and send this as your first prompt.
Then tell me in the comments: what's the first app you'll build?
Next time: a tour inside a Rayfin app, and the building blocks it can grow. See you in the water!
Psst… my eyes are on top, and my mouth is underneath. So I can watch while I eat!
